cells.purpose: Map the checkpoint's architecture name to the Llama pipeline implementation.

notes.title: Architecture key
notes.text: Lookup uses the architecture name. The example repository IDs are examples, while dimensions come from the selected checkpoint.

notes.title: Implementation and adapters
notes.text: The registration supplies the pipeline model, tokenizer, supported encodings, and weight adapters.

cells.purpose: Coordinate model settings, graph recipes, compilation, and initialization.

notes.title: Resolve the model
notes.text: Read/adapt weights, resolve config, and initialize any distributed runtime required by the selected graph.

notes.title: Trace, compile, initialize
notes.text: The helper called here owns tracing as well as compilation and initialization; a GraphSpec is still a recipe.

notes.title: Finish pipeline wiring
notes.text: After initialized models exist, eligible host weights can be released and the batch processor is wired.

cells.purpose: Choose the decoder implementation from parallelism and device count.

notes.title: Ordered selection
notes.text: Data parallel takes priority, then multiple-device tensor parallel, then the single-device route used here.

cells.purpose: Initialize model settings and resolve weight-dependent configuration.

notes.title: Two configuration steps
notes.text: Initialize reads pipeline/HF settings; finalize receives checkpoint state plus output and normalization policy.

cells.purpose: Resolve quantization, projection layout, tied weights, and output policy.

notes.title: Normalize names for inspection
notes.text: Use canonical Llama-style keys when inspecting checkpoint metadata. This local normalized mapping supports subsequent feature detection.

notes.title: Inspect metadata
notes.text: Quantization and normalization information are derived from config and weights before graph modules are constructed.

notes.title: Commit resolved settings
notes.text: The final fields include tied embeddings, stacked MLP/QKV projections, attention bias, and output policy.

cells.purpose: Package the Llama module, input contract, and weight registry into a recipe.

notes.title: Module then recipe
notes.text: The module is constructed and weights are loaded before the named input tree and registry are packaged in GraphSpec.

cells.purpose: Assemble the Llama decoder layers from the resolved configuration.

notes.title: Position encoding
notes.text: RoPE configuration includes head count, hidden size, sequence limit, and the target device.

notes.title: Encoding-specific modules
notes.text: Linear, attention, and MLP implementations are chosen from quantization and stacked-projection settings.

notes.title: Repeated decoder blocks
notes.text: Each block receives attention, MLP, normalization, and KV parameters. The layer count comes from config.

notes.title: Input/output projections
notes.text: Embedding and language-model head dimensions follow config. The output weight can be shared with the embedding.

cells.purpose: Record the attention and MLP residual paths for one decoder block.

notes.title: Attention path
notes.text: Normalize the incoming hidden states and call attention with layer index, KV collection, RoPE data, and sequence boundaries.

notes.title: Two residual additions
notes.text: The attention output joins x; the normalized result goes through MLP and joins h. Optional multipliers are explicit branches.

cells.purpose: Trace the configured layer sequence, then process logits.

notes.title: Python expands the layer structure
notes.text: Each call uses symbolic tensors while tracing. Layer index constants and KV/row-offset inputs are attached to the recorded computation.

notes.title: Decoder output policy
notes.text: The final hidden states are passed to the common logits/output-tree construction path.

cells.purpose: Select output positions, normalize them, and project to vocabulary logits.

notes.title: Last-token positions
notes.text: Row offsets identify each sequence's final token. The model gathers those rows before normalization and the language-model head.

notes.title: Static output-policy branches
notes.text: The configured policy selects extra variable-count or all-token logits. return_n_logits supplies values used by the variable path.

notes.title: Named outputs
notes.text: Logits, offsets, and optional hidden states form the output tree later flattened by Graph.output.

cells.purpose: Declare symbolic batch tensor types and placements.

notes.title: Packed tokens and boundaries
notes.text: Tokens are int64; row offsets are uint32. Both use the selected device, with symbolic lengths.

notes.title: Host-side count input
notes.text: This count tensor is int64 on CPU; its symbolic length is declared independently from the token count.

cells.purpose: Flatten the input-type tree and dispatch to the module's trace method.

notes.title: Variant boundary
notes.text: The ModuleV3 branch stages differently. The Graph API route continues to self.module.trace below.

notes.title: Preserve recipe settings
notes.text: The graph name, module container, extensions, and device-graph flag are passed with the flattened type leaves.

cells.purpose: Adapt flat graph inputs back into the Llama forward contract.

notes.title: Recover KV structure
notes.text: The graph boundary is flat; this adapter reconstructs the per-device KV collection required by the model.

notes.title: Trace through the constructor
notes.text: Passing forward to Graph causes the constructor to invoke it on symbolic graph inputs and finalize its returned outputs.

cells.purpose: Create MLIR graph structure and optionally trace a Python callable.

notes.title: Symbolic dimensions
notes.text: Names from symbolic tensor/buffer dimensions become graph parameters.

notes.title: MLIR ownership
notes.text: Use a supplied module or create one, then create mo.graph with input types and initially empty result types.

notes.title: Kernel declarations and graph mode
notes.text: Import the kernel library and mark the graph if explicit device-graph construction was requested.

notes.title: Automatic finalization
notes.text: Run the callable inside the active graph context. Its return form determines how output is invoked.

cells.purpose: Finish the graph's output contract and verify the completed graph.

notes.title: 1 · Flatten outputs
notes.text: Retain the Python output structure; flatten its leaves. A string leaf is rejected because unpacking a dict into its keys is usually a mistake.

notes.title: 2 · Normalize values and chains
notes.text: Convert leaves to Graph Values and include final chain values when the graph has chain inputs. Chains preserve dependency ordering.

notes.title: 3 · Set both signatures
notes.text: The actual argument and result types define functionType and the kgen generator signature. Symbolic dimensions can remain symbolic.

notes.title: 4 · Append the terminator
notes.text: mo.output identifies which SSA values leave the graph. This records IR; it does not launch inference.

notes.title: 5 · Name the interface
notes.text: Ordinal input/result names are written for the engine. The Python output tree is retained separately.

notes.title: 6 · Verify the graph
notes.text: Clear temporary bookkeeping and invoke MLIR graph verification. Failure reports diagnostics. Numerical correctness and target compilation remain separate checks.

cells.purpose: Exit the active graph-construction context.

notes.title: Context restoration
notes.text: This delegates context exit; output signature construction and native compilation occur elsewhere.

cells.purpose: Set and restore the active graph while Python operations are recorded.

notes.title: Scoped graph state
notes.text: The finally block restores the previous graph even when construction raises an exception.

cells.purpose: Read a complete existing test that builds an add graph and checks interface metadata.

notes.title: Finalization in a small graph
notes.text: This explicit output call establishes the result contract; the following assertions inspect its names.

cells.purpose: Trace graph recipes, compile artifacts, then initialize their weights.

notes.title: Trace each compilation group
notes.text: The ordinary Llama decoder has one spec. Multiple grouped roles can instead share a graph Module.

notes.title: Compilation boundary
notes.text: The completed graph or module is compiled or resolved through configured artifact reuse.

notes.title: Bind after compilation
notes.text: Collect weights by name, reject conflicting values, and initialize all models in the compiled artifact.

cells.purpose: Select normal compilation, configured MEF import, or MEF export.

notes.title: Choose the store
notes.text: Use the explicit session store if present, otherwise the default. Non-Graph modules take the regular compile route.

notes.title: Import or decline
notes.text: A matching artifact path is passed to compile. A store that declines this graph falls back to compiling the graph.

notes.title: Export mode
notes.text: Write the compiled artifact under the store's claimed export location.

cells.purpose: Prepare a Graph, Module, or artifact path for asynchronous native compilation.

notes.title: Source-kind dispatch
notes.text: Paths and in-memory Graphs follow different branches. A Graph contributes its MLIR module and extension libraries.

notes.title: Retain initialization expectations
notes.text: The graph's weight declarations supply expected device metadata, checked when weight buffers are bound.

notes.title: Seed declarations
notes.text: Reuse kernel declarations already loaded by the Graph's KernelLibrary before the native module handoff.

notes.title: Return an artifact handle
notes.text: The handle carries the asynchronous result and graph names. compile() below waits for completion.

cells.purpose: Wait for asynchronous compilation and surface errors to the caller.

notes.title: Synchronous completion
notes.text: Schedule compilation, wait on its result, and distinguish requested pre-JIT stopping from a compile failure.

cells.purpose: Cross the Python/C++ boundary with the MLIR module capsule.

notes.title: Serialize native compilation
notes.text: The process-wide lock is acquired before scheduling. Synchronous setup errors release it immediately.

notes.title: Payload
notes.text: The capsule identifies the MLIR module; extensions, a pipeline name, and the fusion option accompany it.

notes.title: Asynchronous lifetime
notes.text: Completion releases the lock through a callback. Returning a pending handle does not end the protected compile interval.

cells.purpose: Turn the Python module capsule into a native CompilationRequest.

notes.title: Opaque source and format
notes.text: The frontend must interpret the pointer using the matching MLIR implementation and file format.

notes.title: Schedule engine compilation
notes.text: Hand the populated request to the engine and return its asynchronous result.

cells.purpose: Schedule compilation on a CPU worker and resolve an asynchronous result.

notes.title: Worker boundary
notes.text: The captured request is processed by compileModelSync on the CPU worker; error and telemetry handling resolve the returned handle.

cells.purpose: Supply device configuration and create native compiled-model objects.

notes.title: Target context
notes.text: Pass configured devices into the compilation request, then dispatch to CompiledModels::create.

cells.purpose: Compile in-memory source or read a model artifact from a path.

notes.title: Graph-source branch
notes.text: A source pointer selects the MOF frontend, which produces a MEF buffer. read then builds compiled-model objects from that buffer.

notes.title: Already compiled path
notes.text: A MEF path is read directly. Entering an API named compile does not imply compiler passes run.

cells.purpose: Clone the graph module, configure lowering, and consult the native MEF cache.

notes.title: Compiler-owned module
notes.text: Lowering transforms a clone of the incoming module. Weight resources are owned by its MLIR context.

notes.title: Resolve compiler options
notes.text: Collect configuration and detect pre-seeded kernel declarations before deriving cache behavior.

notes.title: Cache-hit return
notes.text: When model-IR caching is enabled and a matching artifact exists, return it before convertMOToMEF runs.

notes.title: Cache miss
notes.text: Compile/serialize, then attempt to insert the resulting buffer in the cache.

cells.purpose: Run graph compilation, then serialize the lowered model to MEF.

notes.title: Execute compiler passes
notes.text: A failed pipeline returns graph diagnostics rather than an artifact.

notes.title: Intentional early stop
notes.text: Pre-JIT inspection ends after Mojo emission; the partially lowered result is not serialized to the MEF cache.

notes.title: Artifact boundary
notes.text: Serialize the successfully lowered module and return its MEF buffer.

cells.purpose: Prepare and optimize high-level graph operations before MAP lowering.

notes.title: Kernel definitions
notes.text: Import/verify packages only when declarations were not already seeded by the caller.

notes.title: Shape and symbolic work
notes.text: Shape inference and constant folding are configured independently; symbolic optimization and cleanup run in this stage.

notes.title: Layouts and optional patterns
notes.text: Infer layouts and optionally run named pattern fusion before validating device information.

notes.title: Target legality
notes.text: Check device information before the final cleanup and unused-operation removal.

cells.purpose: Fuse eligible structured computations and outline kernel bodies.

notes.title: Structural fusion
notes.text: Fusion is a transformation of eligible graph structure. The schedule alone does not prove which Llama operations fuse.

notes.title: Output storage
notes.text: Provide accumulating buffers after fusion, including mixed-precision handling.

notes.title: Outline bodies
notes.text: Create structured kernel bodies after view handling, then simplify their captures and invariant views.

cells.purpose: Legalize kernel calls and outline routines.

notes.title: Call preparation
notes.text: Legalize rowwise kernels, conform operands, outline routines, and add tracing wrappers before module cleanup.

cells.purpose: Plan runtime resources, lower primitives, and emit Mojo routines.

notes.title: Memory planning
notes.text: Buffer reuse, allocation planning, deferral, and argument validation operate on the runtime-model representation.

notes.title: Device-graph path
notes.text: Staging, dependency computation, build stubs, and finalization are separate from the frontend Graph.output operation.

notes.title: Deduplicate routines
notes.text: Earlier canonicalization makes equivalent routines eligible for merging. Layer count is not necessarily the count of distinct generated routines.

notes.title: Emit source for JIT
notes.text: Mojo emission is at the end of this builder. The enclosing pipeline schedules kernel JIT afterward.

cells.purpose: Build the ordered sequence of representation conversions and compiler stages.

notes.title: High-level graph stage
notes.text: The mo-pre-map dump follows MO processing; subsequent stage names distinguish conversions from stage-local transforms.

notes.title: Representation transition
notes.text: Stable-tensor marking precedes MO-to-MAP conversion.

notes.title: Kernel representation
notes.text: MOGG preparation precedes conversion into the MGP runtime model.

notes.title: JIT configuration
notes.text: JIT target and compilation options are only configured when JIT is enabled.

notes.title: Compile kernels
notes.text: After MGP/Mojo emission, run JIT compilation, strip kernel declarations, and finish runtime-call lowering.

cells.purpose: Construct the pass manager and run the configured compiler pipeline.

notes.title: Build then execute
notes.text: Adding passes describes the schedule. pm.run applies that schedule to the module and returns success or failure.

cells.purpose: Finalize collectives only for an MGP model marked as a device graph.

notes.title: Explicit gate
notes.text: An unmarked model returns immediately. The pass's name refers to device-graph collectives, not Python graph output finalization.

notes.title: Finalize each collective
notes.text: Failures from collective finalization signal a compiler pass failure.

cells.purpose: Validate weight buffers and initialize models in a compiled artifact.

notes.title: Weight contract
notes.text: Check names and expected CPU/device category captured from the graph. These checks occur after graph finalization and compilation.

notes.title: Buffer layout check
notes.text: Non-contiguous registered weights are rejected with the offending weight's name.

notes.title: Native initialization
notes.text: Bind the registry through the native load path; return models keyed by their names.

cells.purpose: Create executable model instances once compilation resolves.

notes.title: Initialize on a runtime worker
notes.text: The continuation uses the compiled artifact and captured weight registry on the CPU runtime worker.

notes.title: Executable state
notes.text: Create the executable models with runtime configuration and actual weight buffers, then resolve the result.

cells.purpose: Execute an initialized decoder on the current batch's buffers.

notes.title: Per-batch call
notes.text: Prepared token/KV buffers enter the existing model. The batch processor interprets its output buffers.
